intent: Hold the iteration-2 geometry unchanged for the final race: five 16 mm sensors at x = -0.05 to +0.05 m, y = 0.04 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body 0.12 x 0.18 m, mass 0.8 kg. This is the best-scoring geometry, it has zero line loss on the oval and slalom, and every geometry lever tested has been shown to leave max_error unchanged. I am not making a geometry change without a supported hypothesis, because the final unseen track is scored once and cannot be re-run. I am asking the Integrator to report where in the run max_error peaks, since that is the only evidence that would justify a geometry change in a later round.
learning: Ten iterations of geometry tests show that span is the only sensing lever that changes line loss, and that no tested geometry (footprint, y, wheel_track, mass, wheel_radius, body) moves the roughly 0.061 m excursion. If the final race shows the excursion disappears under the controller change, the remaining gain is in control and the geometry should stay fixed. If the excursion persists, the next question is whether it is a start-up transient or a steady bias; the step or bend at which max_error peaks would separate them, and a later geometry proposal would need to name that hypothesis and the measurement that confirms it.
rationale: This is the final iteration, so the design I deliver here is the one that will race the unseen final track, and I have no further iteration to recover from a bad geometry change. The evidence across iterations 0 to 10 supports holding the iteration-2 geometry. Span of ±0.05 m is the only change that mattered: it removed line loss on the oval and slalom (iteration 1). Footprint (12 vs 16 mm), wheel_track (0.10, 0.12, 0.15 m), mass (0.6 vs 0.8 kg), wheel_radius (0.03 vs 0.04 m, where 0.04 m scored worse) and sensor y (0.02 and 0.04 m identical; 0.06 m reintroduced line loss) all left max_error at about 0.061 m. The off-track floor is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), and the widest allowed body gives only 0.0575 m, so no body change can lift it. The Integrator asked me to hold this geometry, and I took that advice. Their feedback also says that no tested geometry lever explains the excursion, and that a further geometry change needs a named start-up hypothesis with its confirming measurement. I have no such hypothesis with evidence behind it, so I do not add an untested change to the final race. I also note that iteration 10 (controller base-speed change, same geometry) raised the score to 27.3854, with oval max_error moving slightly, so the excursion may be partly speed-dependent. That is the Integrator's lever to tune, not a reason to change the sensing geometry now. Expected result: the same behaviour as the best row, about 26.99 to 27.39 depending on the controller, with zero line loss and max_error near 0.061 m on the development tracks.
